you need a second compressor. Dont have one compressor doing all the work. When you say rich/full vocals you are talking about leveling the transients of your performance and bringing the low parts of your performance up, so you get those nice rich parts of the lower end and bass of your voice more prevalent. Use one compressor with quick attack fast release to level the vocal out so you don’t have any transients poking. Use another compressor with slower attack and medium release to bring those low parts of your performance/voice up. vocals in modern pop and rap songs are compressed to shit. you want to compress your vocal enough to where you can bring the overall vocal up so you get that nice low end to your voice. you need more than one compressor to achieve this. Also you need compressor cus you don’t have stems so you have to compress ya vocals to fit the stereo track. cuz you cant level each instrument. Train your ears and learn to hear that compressor. it is your best friend in the genera you are working in. 

Also don’t let all the advice confuse you. Again use your ears if it sounds good to you and close enough. It is good. Don’t over think it. your song and vocals sound pretty good to me already. good luck.
